minutes.headline: Select Board approved FY26 budget amendments; deferred action after a newly surfaced Fitchburg water billing shortfall
minutes.summary: The select board reviewed and unanimously recommended approval of Article 2, amending the FY2026 omnibus budget to cover town accountant transition costs, audit costs, and contracted services, funded partly by salary reserve transfers. Discussion of Article 3 (payment of prior year bills) uncovered a long-standing failure to properly bill City of Fitchburg water customers, resulting in a large accrued bill with interest; the board deferred a recommendation on that article until its meeting the next day, ahead of special town meeting.

what_happened.line: The board found a long-standing failure to properly bill City of Fitchburg water customers, leaving an accrued balance with interest, and put off a recommendation on paying it.
The board unanimously recommended approval of an amendment to the FY2026 town budget covering town accountant transition costs, audit costs, and contracted services.
Officials raised switching Fitchburg water billing from quarterly to monthly to cut down on interest charges, without a formal vote.
The board will take up a water rate adjustment at a future meeting.
A tri-board meeting was confirmed for November 24th.

why_it_matters: Residents served by City of Fitchburg water may face a bill reflecting years of under-billing plus interest, and a possible shift to monthly billing.
The budget amendment funds town accountant, audit, and finance-office costs and goes to special town meeting for a vote.
A future water rate adjustment could change what water customers pay going forward.
watch_next: The board's meeting the day after this one, ahead of special town meeting, where Article 3 (payment of prior year bills, including the Fitchburg water billing) is due for a recommendation.
